### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c`**
   - The order of operations in the `mlx5_ib_unbind_slave_port` function has been modified. 
   - The spinlock (`mpi_lock`) is now released before unregistering the notifier (`mlx5_notifier_unregister`), which was previously done while the lock was held.
   - The line that sets `mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call` to `NULL` has been moved to occur after the notifier unregister call, ensuring that the notifier is unregistered before the pointer is cleared.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The primary relationship between the modifications is that they address a kernel panic issue caused by holding a spinlock during the notifier unregister sequence. By releasing the spinlock before unregistering the notifier, the patch prevents the scheduling while atomic bug, thereby improving the stability of the system when using bond mode LACP with GRE tunnels. The changes ensure that the notifier is properly unregistered without holding the lock, which is crucial for avoiding deadlocks and ensuring proper scheduling.

Fixes: df097a278c75 ("IB/mlx5: Use the new mlx5 core notifier API")
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@mellanox.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190731083852.584-1-leon@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Doug Ledford <dledford@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by not releasing the spinlock during the notifier unregister sequence in the `mlx5_ib_unbind_slave_port` function, which led to a kernel panic due to scheduling while atomic. This situation occurs when a thread attempts to sleep while holding a lock, violating the atomic context rules of the kernel.

Here is the patch:
 /* The mlx5_ib_multiport_mutex should be held when calling this function */
 static void mlx5_ib_unbind_slave_port(struct mlx5_ib_dev *ibdev,
 				      struct mlx5_ib_multiport_info *mpi)
 {
 	u8 port_num = mlx5_core_native_port_num(mpi->mdev) - 1;
 	struct mlx5_ib_port *port = &ibdev->port[port_num];
 	int comps;
 	int err;
 	int i;
 
 	mlx5_ib_cleanup_cong_debugfs(ibdev, port_num);
 
 	spin_lock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 	if (!mpi->ibdev) {
 		spin_unlock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 		return;
 	}
 
-	if (mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call)
-		mlx5_notifier_unregister(mpi->mdev, &mpi->mdev_events);
-	mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call = NULL;
-
 	mpi->ibdev = NULL;
 
 	spin_unlock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
+	if (mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call)
+		mlx5_notifier_unregister(mpi->mdev, &mpi->mdev_events);
+	mpi->mdev_events.notifier_call = NULL;
 	mlx5_remove_netdev_notifier(ibdev, port_num);
 	spin_lock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 
 	comps = mpi->mdev_refcnt;
 	if (comps) {
 		mpi->unaffiliate = true;
 		init_completion(&mpi->unref_comp);
 		spin_unlock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 
 		for (i = 0; i < comps; i++)
 			wait_for_completion(&mpi->unref_comp);
 
 		spin_lock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 		mpi->unaffiliate = false;
 	}
 
 	port->mp.mpi = NULL;
 
 	list_add_tail(&mpi->list, &mlx5_ib_unaffiliated_port_list);
 
 	spin_unlock(&port->mp.mpi_lock);
 
 	err = mlx5_nic_vport_unaffiliate_multiport(mpi->mdev);
 
 	mlx5_ib_dbg(ibdev, "unaffiliated port %d\n", port_num + 1);
 	/* Log an error, still needed to cleanup the pointers and add
 	 * it back to the list.
 	 */
 	if (err)
 		mlx5_ib_err(ibdev, "Failed to unaffiliate port %u\n",
 			    port_num + 1);
 
 	ibdev->port[port_num].roce.last_port_state = IB_PORT_DOWN;
 }
